title: Career Fields and Study Skills
summary: Linking interests, abilities and subjects to career fields, sources of career information, admission requirements, and effective study and time-management skills for the FET phase.

notes.text: Career choice begins with self-knowledge: your **interests** (what you enjoy), **abilities** (what you are good at), **personality** and **values**. Tools such as interest questionnaires (e.g. the Holland codes: Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising, Conventional) can help.

items: Universities set **APS** (Admission Point Score) and subject requirements; e.g. engineering usually needs Mathematics and Physical Sciences.
**TVET colleges** offer vocational programmes (NC(V) and N-courses) in fields such as engineering, hospitality and office administration.
**Learnerships** and **apprenticeships** combine study and work, funded through SETAs.
Check requirements early, so that your subject marks in Grades 10–12 keep your options open.

notes.title: Checking the requirements
notes.problem: A university course needs Mathematics at Level 5. Lindo is getting 55%. Is he on track?
notes.answer: No. He needs at least 60%, and to seek extra support.

items: Use a weekly **timetable** with short study sessions and breaks.
Study **actively**: summaries, mind maps, flash cards and self-testing.
Space out revision over weeks (spaced practice) instead of cramming.
Practise past papers under exam conditions.
Look after sleep, nutrition and exercise.

notes.label: Time management
notes.text: Prioritise with the urgent–important matrix: do **urgent and important** tasks now (assignment due tomorrow), **schedule important but not urgent** ones (revision for next month's test), and limit time-wasters (endless scrolling).

notes.title: Making a mind map
notes.problem: How do you make a mind map on a topic such as the water cycle?
steps: Write the topic in the middle.
notes.answer: One central idea, branches and keywords.

questions.prompt: Using the urgent–important matrix, how should you handle revision for a test in four weeks' time?
questions.memo:

questions.prompt: Why should Grade 10 learners research career requirements early?
questions.memo:
✓ To make sure their subjects and marks meet entry requirements (1)
✓ and to set goals and keep options open (1)
